newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Thin Australian stocks end down as Dow drops.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Thin Australian stocks end down as Dow drops.

text.p: *Stocks end weaker but well off lows despite diving with Dow early. Turnover stays light. Total volume 200.75 million, value A$284.43 million, 936 stocks traded, 279 steady, 433 up, 224 down.
Australian shares closed weaker but well off their lows on Thursday as a thinly traded market started the New Year.

Despite diving 27 points early after the Dow's dip on Tuesday, strong support below the 2,400 level saw the local bourse bounce back and spend most of its day trading in a five point range between 2,410 and 2,415.

At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.4 points lower at 2411.2 after touching an intraday low of 2,397.8. March share price index futures were down 13 points at 2,436 and were at a 24.8 point premium to the underlying index.
"The Dow fall went through and then people started to pick it up again," said a Melbourne-based dealer.
An upbeat local tone ensured any Dow-inspired losses were minimised with the relatively strong Australian performance of the last few days continuing.
"It has looked pretty good. The year ended well and that was quite positive even though trade has been pretty quiet." he said.
The holiday lull was seen continuing with little fresh information or data likely to stir a largely inactive market.
"There is no real economic news due out in the next couple of days so I think people may be just treading water," the dealer said.
With the leaders seeing little interest, attention switched to the smaller end of the market with several Gawler Craton explorers attracting interest.
Minotaur Gold, up seven percent, and Merritt Mining, up six percent, were the pick of the bunch.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade remained slow in line with underlying markets although futures activity was buoyant as players set themselves in the new March contract.
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 5,958 (3,414)

In other local markets, Australian bonds failed to break out of their holiday torpor with several centres staying closed within the Asia region, although yields were higher reflecting weakness in the U.S. prior to the New Year holiday. By 4.35 p.m. (0535 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.48 percent.

The Australian dollar started 1997 on a subdued note, held to a narrow range as holidays in other centres hampered liquidity and interest. By 4.35 p.m. (0535 GMT) the unit was motionless at US$0.7941/46, level with an early US$0.7942/52.
